questions.q: What port does mongod listen on by default?
questions.explain: MongoDB's default port is 27017, the equivalent of SQL Server's default 1433.

questions.q: On Windows, what happens when you install MongoDB Community Server via the MSI installer?
options: It can register mongod as a Windows Service, so it starts automatically with the machine
It only runs when Compass is open
It requires manually compiling the source code
It installs only the shell, with no server component
questions.explain: The MSI installer offers to register MongoDB as a Windows Service — no separate manual start step needed.

questions.q: In `docker run --name mongodb -d -p 27017:27017 -v mongodb-data:/data/db mongo`, what does the `-v mongodb-data:/data/db` flag accomplish?
options: Mounts a named Docker volume for the data directory, so data survives a container restart
Verifies the image's checksum before running
Verbosely logs every database write to the console
questions.explain: Without a mounted volume for /data/db, deleting the container deletes the data stored inside it too.

options: MongoDB's free, official GUI client for browsing and querying data — the closest equivalent to SSMS
A third-party paid tool with no affiliation to MongoDB
The name of MongoDB's cloud hosting service
A command-line-only tool with no visual interface
questions.explain: Compass is MongoDB's own free, official GUI — this lesson frames it as the SSMS-equivalent for a relational DBA.

questions.q: What connection string would you use in Compass to connect to a default local MongoDB install or the Docker container from this lesson?
questions.explain: mongodb://localhost:27017 is the standard connection string for a local server on MongoDB's default port.
